fact: subsection heading "Decision rule and familywise error" + label
MC p value is (k+1)/(B+1), k of B null pseudo-experiments reach the observed statistic
probe: The Monte Carlo $p$ value of a test is $(k+1)/(B+1)$, where $k$ of $B$ null pseudo-experiments reach the observed statistic.

fact: the p value is never zero
probe: reach the observed statistic. This $p$ value is never zero.

fact: each decision uses the largest p over a set of shifted nulls
probe: the $p$ value used for the decision is the largest over these shifts and need not come from the one shown

fact: a shifted null adds a fixed vector to every null draw
probe: Each shifted null adds the same fixed vector $s$ to every null draw before the statistic is formed

fact: shifts are zero, half or all of D, or +-kappa delta_fine
probe: to every null draw before the statistic is formed, with $s\in\{0,\tfrac12D,D,+\jtMoneKappa\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}},-\jtMoneKappa\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}\}$

fact: D is an upper bound on the simulation-size difference (condition iv)
probe: The variants move it by an upper bound on the simulation-size difference between the pseudo-experiments and the data unfold (condition~(iv) below)

fact: D is taken along the null's bias direction
probe: along the null's bias direction it is not always consistent with zero

fact: delta_fine = change of the noise-free unfolded result in the last refinement step of the null truth grid (condition i)
probe: Here $\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$ is the change of the noise-free unfolded result when the null truth is refined from the twofold-merged grid to the fine grid.
remark: note names the step: twofold-merged grid to fine grid

fact: ten tests controlled by Holm at familywise alpha = \jtAlpha
probe: The ten tests are carried out with the Holm procedure~\cite{Holm:1979} at familywise level $\alpha=\jtAlpha$.

fact: pseudo-experiments drawn sequentially, at most \jtBcap per null
probe: Calibration proceeded in batches of \jtBatch{} pseudo-experiments per null, to at most \jtBcap{}, under a sequential rule

fact: reject only when the upper end of the two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson interval of the exceedance fraction lies below the Holm threshold
probe: a step rejects only when the 95\% Clopper--Pearson interval~\cite{Clopper:1934} of $k/B$ lies entirely below its Holm threshold.

fact: the decision uses the upper end of the two-sided 95% interval
probe: The decision rule uses the upper end of the two-sided 95\% interval, a one-sided 97.5\% upper bound.

fact: A1: each true null's calibrated tail probability is uniform or conservative
probe: (A1) each true null's calibrated tail probability is uniformly distributed or conservative

fact: A2: exceedances are independent given the data
probe: (A2) the pseudo-experiments' exceedances are independent given the data

fact: under A1, A2 the probability of meeting the criterion at any B up to \jtBcap is below the threshold
probe: the probability that this upper end falls below the threshold, at any number of pseudo-experiments up to \jtBcap{}, is below the threshold.

fact: whatever rule determines when sampling stops
probe: This holds whatever rule determines when sampling stops, including the budget extensions.

fact: the decision rule controls the FWER of the ten decisions at 5%
probe: The decision rule therefore controls the familywise error rate of the ten decisions at 5\% under these assumptions.

fact: derivation in note appendix sec:joint5d-fwer
probe: This derivation supports the familywise statement of \S\ref{sec:joint5d-frozen}.

fact: calibrated size is averaged over the nuisance priors; at fixed nuisance values it can exceed alpha
probe: The calibrated size is averaged over the nuisance priors: at a fixed true value of the nuisance parameters it can exceed $\alpha$.

fact: the error control applies to the decisions, not separately to the point estimates (k+1)/(B+1)
remark: searched "not separately", "point estimate", "applies to the decisions", "(k+1)/(B+1)" in all sec_*/app_*/main_note; the note says the rule controls FWER "of the ten decisions" but never disclaims control of the p-value point estimates

fact: calibration valid for the simulated null to the extent the pseudo-experiment chain reproduces the analysis of the data
probe: The calibration is valid for the simulated null to the extent that the pseudo-experiment chain reproduces the analysis applied to the data.

fact: this fidelity is assumption A1
probe: The bound rests on A1, the calibration's fidelity, which \S\ref{sec:joint5d-conditions} discusses, and on A2.

fact: every pseudo-experiment resamples the same simulated events
probe: Every pseudo-experiment resamples the same simulated events, so the null distributions are conditional on that simulation.

fact: measuring a rejection rate for null pseudo-data processed like the data would require an independent simulation sample
probe: No rejection rate has been measured for null pseudo-data processed like the data, which would require an independent simulation sample.
remark: note does not join the two clauses causally ("so"); each clause prints

fact: no such rejection rate has been measured
probe: No rejection rate has been measured for null pseudo-data processed like the data

fact: test design fixed before any observed statistic was computed
probe: variants, multiplicity rule, stopping rule and every input were fixed before any production pseudo-experiment or observed statistic, with two data-informed elements.

fact: after descriptive per-cell residuals of the data had been seen
probe: First, the design's reviewers had seen descriptive per-cell residuals of the data before it was fixed.

fact: computing budget extended by a bounded amount after observed p values were visible
probe: Second, a bounded extension of the production budget was decided during production, while the calibration's monitoring output showed observed claim $p$ values

fact: under A1, A2 the error control holds for any stopping rule, so the extension does not affect it
probe: No statistic, variant, threshold or stopping rule was changed, and the familywise bound above holds whatever rule determined when sampling stopped.
remark: including the budget extensions also printed in the FWER sentence (row 93 probe)

fact: \jtLostCal calibration and \jtLostPow power pseudo-experiments did not complete within computing time limits
probe: Computing time limits interrupted or prevented \jtLostCal{} of the submitted calibration pseudo-experiments

probe: never started) and \jtLostPow{} power pseudo-experiments. The decisions in Table~\ref{tab:joint5d} were evaluated on the completed draws.

fact: so their outcomes change no decision
probe: so no assignment of the lost draws changes any decision.

fact: A2 requires the lost pseudo-experiments to be lost independently of their outcomes; not shown
probe: A2 requires the lost pseudo-experiments to have been lost independently of their outcomes, which has not been shown.
